saw_lines: Shoppers trying a new supermarket want one clear reason to switch, then judge the price and the first basket before they commit.
So the first order offer has to sit in the opening line, because that is where a trial is won or lost.
Your site offers a first order discount, yet 0 of 30 ads mention it, so put it in the opening line of three new ads.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 27 Oct 2026
points: Your site offers a first order discount, yet 0 of 30 ads mention it, so a new buyer has no reason to act. Put the discount in the opening line of three new ads, so every viewer sees it first.

Your ads never say how it arrives, and 0 of 30 cover delivery, so buyers who cannot picture the box scroll past. Shoot one video of it arriving at the door, and open with that answer in the first three seconds.

None of your 30 ads carries a proof number, so a first time buyer has nothing concrete to trust before clicking. Collect one real figure, like your review count or orders shipped, and lead the next three ads with it.

All 30 ads use one Learn more button, yet they send buyers to 8 different landing pages, so clicks land unexpectedly. Match each label to its page, Shop now for Halloween and Find a store for the new store opening.

ads_1: Three new video ads opening with the first order discount and a delivery answer
soc_1: Brand social strategy across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and X
